bill.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to the authority of Congress and the States to regulate contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections and to enact public financing systems for political campaigns.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment authorizing Congress and the states to (1) regulate and impose reasonable viewpoint-neutral limitations on the raising and spending of money by candidates and others to influence elections; and (2) regulate and enact public campaign financing systems, including those designed to restrict the influence of private wealth by offsetting the raising and spending of money by candidates and others with increased public funding. The amendment grants Congress and the states the power to implement and enforce this amendment by legislation. They are allowed to distinguish between natural persons and corporations or other artificial entities created by law, including by prohibiting such entities from spending money to influence elections.

classification.plainSummary: This proposed constitutional amendment would allow Congress and state legislatures to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit them to create public financing systems for campaigns and to treat corporations differently from individual people, including by prohibiting corporations from spending money on elections. The amendment would give lawmakers the authority to write laws implementing these changes.

industries.rationale: The amendment would directly regulate how advocacy organizations raise and spend money to influence elections.
The amendment would reshape campaign-finance law and likely generate substantial litigation and compliance work for law firms and lobbying practices.
Regulations on election-related spending could affect advertising revenue and the market for political communications services.
New restrictions on corporate election spending and potential public financing systems could affect financial institutions' political engagement and compliance obligations.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would propose a constitutional amendment authorizing Congress and the states to (1) regulate and impose reasonable viewpoint-neutral limitations on the raising and spending of money by candidates and others to influence elections; and (2) regulate and enact public campaign financing systems. That includes those designed to restrict the influence of private wealth by offsetting the raising and spending of money by candidates and others with increased public funding.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who deals with a federal agency.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in dealing with the government. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
